headline: GOLDMINING'S LA MINA HITS $1.8B NPV AT SPOT PRICES — 152 koz/yr AuEq Over 11-Year Life in Colombia
snippet: GoldMining Inc. (TSX: GOLD; NYSE American: GLDG) filed the NI 43-101 technical report for its La Mina copper-gold project PEA today, confirming base-case economics of a US$1.0 billion after-tax NPV5% at a conservative $1,750/oz gold assumption with a 32.2% IRR and 2.7-year payback. At current spot prices (approx. $4,775/oz Au, $5.75/lb Cu), after-tax NPV swells to $1.8 billion with a 49.1% IRR and 1.9-year payback — on a 11.2-year mine life averaging 152,400 AuEq oz per year from an open-pit operation in Colombia's Antioquia department. Initial capex is estimated at $523 million.

headline: 100 DAYS IN — Iran War's Full Toll on Gold, Oil, and Markets: What the Charts Actually Show
snippet: CNBC's 100-day retrospective on the US-Israel military operation against Iran finds crude oil locked near $96/bbl — roughly 37% above the $70/bbl budget assumptions baked into most gold and copper miner 2026 guidance — while gold initially surged to $5,400 before retreating 15% as markets framed the conflict as a temporary demand shock rather than a structural monetary shift. Defense spending and nuclear energy have been the unexpected equity winners over the conflict period; uranium equities outperformed gold miners by a wide margin in the same window.

headline: GOLD ETF EXODUS IN MAY — First Monthly Outflow Since November as Rate-Hike Repricing Sidelines Buyers
snippet: Global physically-backed gold ETFs recorded US$2 billion in net outflows in May 2026 — the first monthly redemption since November 2025 — as rangebound gold prices, renewed risk appetite, and higher opportunity costs from US dollar strength and elevated rate expectations sidelined institutional buyers. North America shed US$1.5 billion and Asia US$489 million; Europe was the sole region with inflows (+US$225 million) on fiscal and political uncertainty. Total AUM fell 1% to US$374 billion, with holdings at 4,121 tonnes — just shy of February's record high. Year-to-date flows remain positive at nearly US$17 billion.

headline: SILVER SLUMPED 6% POST-PAYROLLS — But the Structural Deficit That's Drained 762 Million Ounces Since 2021 Hasn't Moved
snippet: GoldSilver.com argues the 6% silver price plunge following May's 172,000-job payroll beat represents speculative positioning washout, not a change in silver's underlying supply dynamics: the market is entering its sixth consecutive annual deficit — a projected 46.3 million ounce shortfall in 2026 widening from 40.3 Moz in 2025 — with a cumulative drawdown since 2021 now standing at 762 million troy ounces. Available silver in London vaults hit a historic low of 17% unencumbered in September 2025, triggering a physical liquidity squeeze; that structural tightness is unchanged by any single economic data print.

headline: MERK: IRAN CONFLICT MARKET SELLOFF IS A 'SHOCK REPRICING,' NOT A STRUCTURAL SHIFT — The Gold Bull Case Is Intact
snippet: Axel Merk, writing via Money Metals Exchange, argues markets are correctly labelling the Iran conflict as a temporary demand shock — not a structural monetary crisis — which is why gold has sold off alongside, rather than rallied through, geopolitical stress: when real yields rise sharply on aggressive rate-hike repricing without a commensurate rise in long-run inflation expectations, gold underperforms regardless of headline risk. Merk's thesis: the structural drivers (central bank de-dollarization, fiscal deterioration, reserve rebalancing away from US Treasuries) are fully intact, and the current selloff is a positioning washout that will reassert once the payroll-shock repricing stabilizes.

headline: METALS FOCUS: GOLD BULL MARKET 'STILL HAS LEGS' — $4,920/oz Average Maintained, Year-High Target Lifted Above $5,000
snippet: Metals Focus, one of the world's leading precious metals research consultancies, maintained its bullish 2026 gold outlook in a report cited by Money Metals Exchange, forecasting a US$4,920/oz full-year average despite the 12% drawdown from January's $5,102 peak. The firm sees the current correction as a speculative positioning washout rather than a trend reversal, pointing to intact structural demand (central bank accumulation at 244 tonnes in Q1 alone), the inflation risk embedded in sustained $90–$100/bbl oil, and regime uncertainty in US policy. Metals Focus raised its year-high target to 'well above $5,000' on expectations that rate-hike repricing will stabilize before the autumn seasonal rally cycle.

headline: NORSEMONT DRILLS 20m AT 1.20 g/t AuEq AT BOTTOM OF HOLE — Choquelimpie System Remains Open at Depth in Northern Chile
snippet: Norsemont Mining Inc. (CSE: NOM) reported Phase 3 drill assays from the Choquelimpie high-sulfidation gold-silver-copper project in Tarapacá Region, northern Chile, including a 20-metre intercept at 1.20 g/t gold equivalent at the bottom of the drill hole — confirming the system remains open at depth. With seven Phase 3 core holes completed (approximately 1,650 metres drilled), the program has now identified three distinct styles of gold mineralization: oxide, hydrothermal breccia, and transitional zones. CEO Marc Levy noted this geological complexity is 'an important step forward' in guiding future high-grade targeting at a project adjacent to major infrastructure.

headline: BEARISH CALL: Analyst Says Gold May Fall to $4,099 — 'Technically Broken' Chart Overrides Fundamental Bull Case
snippet: Against the consensus bullish chorus, at least one technical analyst is flagging meaningful downside for gold: Business Standard's coverage of June 5 analysis warns that XAU/USD has 'technically broken down' and could fall toward the $4,099 level — roughly 5% below Monday's $4,314 close — if the key $4,336 yearly-open support fails on a weekly closing basis. The argument rests on the sharp deterioration in speculative positioning post-payrolls, elevated real yields from the rate-hike repricing, and a dollar index that has not yet fully reflected the 72% year-end rate-hike probability now priced by CME FedWatch. Buyers at current levels are fighting the momentum.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL: MP MATERIALS LEADS USAR — But Serra Verde Acquisition ($2.8B) Is Building a Mine-to-Magnet Rival
snippet: The Motley Fool's June 8 head-to-head analysis of the two leading domestic rare earth plays comes down in favour of MP Materials (NYSE: MP), which produced a record 917 metric tonnes of NdPr in Q1 2026 (up 63% YoY) and posted positive adjusted EBITDA of $36.6M after being negative a year ago. USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR), however, is closing the gap fast: it has completed acquisitions of Brazil's Serra Verde Group (the largest heavy rare earth deposit outside China) for $2.8 billion and UK-based Less Common Metals for $220 million, adding both upstream deposits and downstream separation know-how to its growing mine-to-magnet ambition alongside the $1.6B CHIPS Act award.

headline: AMERICAN EAGLE GOLD KILLS PACIFIC BOOKER BID — Fairness Opinion Rules 31% Premium 'Financially Inadequate'
snippet: American Eagle Gold Corp. (TSXV: AE) terminated its hostile take-over bid for Pacific Booker Minerals (TSXV: BKM) on June 5, abandoning an all-share offer launched April 14 at 1.41 AE shares per BKM share — a 31% premium at announcement — with nearly two months left to run before its scheduled expiry. The catalyst for withdrawal: an independent fairness opinion from INFOR Financial concluded the consideration was financially inadequate, giving BKM's board the ammunition to reject the offer. No BKM shares were taken up; all tendered shares were returned. The failed bid is a signal that premium benchmarks in junior gold M&A are rising alongside the metal price, making all-share offers at headline premiums increasingly vulnerable to fairness challenges.
